intro: Onsite and remote IT support for offices, letting agents, managed blocks and HMOs across the 269 dual-ring towns. Price on application after scope.

Letting agents, block managers, landlords with a site office, small offices and HMO operators who run shared broadband are the usual callers. Most do not want a full in-house IT team. They want a named person who can fix the laptop that will not join the network, the printer that drops off every Monday and the mailbox that stopped syncing, and then write down what was done.

Property businesses have a particular mix of kit: a handful of laptops, a shared printer, a router supplied by the broadband provider, a door-entry or CCTV recorder on the same network, and software for tenancies, rent and maintenance tickets. We look at that whole picture before changing anything, because a fix for one device can break another on a small network.

We do not promise an attendance time, a fix time or a response time on this page. A visit or remote session is proposed when the diary allows, and the written quote is price on application.

p: We work on live business data, so access is agreed in writing. Passwords are set or reset by the client where possible, admin accounts are named, and nothing is copied off site unless the instruction says so. UK GDPR responsibilities stay with the business; we follow the access rules it sets.

urgent-it-support.intro: Urgent IT Support: how urgent requests for IT support are handled by iComply from Stockport, without attendance-time promises.
urgent-it-support.body: IT support covers the day-to-day problems that stop a small office or property business working: laptops that will not start or join Wi-Fi, email that stops syncing, printers that drop off the network, shared drives that cannot be found and accounts that are locked. A typical visit starts with a list of users and devices, then works through the reported faults in order of business impact. Where a fault needs a part, a licence or a third-party supplier, that is named in the note rather than guessed.
urgent-it-support.meta_desc: Urgent IT Support for offices, letting agents and landlords from Stockport. Onsite or remote, written scope, price on application. 269 North West towns.

Fault reproduced and the cause written down
Fix tested with the person who reported it
Handover note of changes and remaining risks
faq: Do you guarantee a time for urgent IT support?
No. We do not publish or promise attendance times. We tell you honestly when someone can help once we know the fault.
What should I do while waiting for urgent help?
Do not keep restarting equipment or deleting files. Note what happened, photograph error messages and leave the affected device as it is unless it is overheating or smoking.
What does IT support from iComply include?

Fault-finding and fixes on laptops, desktops, printers, email, accounts and the office network, onsite or remotely, in the scope agreed on the quote. Hardware, licences and third-party contracts are listed separately.
Do you support Macs as well as Windows?
Yes for common business use: joining the network, email, printers, backups and accounts. Specialist creative or development set-ups are scoped case by case.
Can you work alongside our existing IT provider?
Yes. If another company holds admin access or a contract, we agree who does what before touching anything so that nobody undoes the other's work.
Do you keep our passwords?
The business keeps owner-level access. Where we need admin access we use named accounts and hand them back or disable them at the end.
Can you help with GDPR?
We follow the access and data rules the business sets and can advise on technical measures. Legal compliance stays with the business.

sections.h2: How a urgent IT Support job is scoped
p: When systems stop, the first step is a call with the business owner or site contact so we understand what has failed and what the business cannot work without. Many urgent faults can be contained remotely first, for example by restoring a mailbox, re-enabling an account or bypassing a failed switch. Where a visit is needed, it is proposed when an engineer is free. We do not promise an attendance time, a fix time or a response time on this page. A visit or remote session is proposed when the diary allows, and the written quote is price on application. If we cannot help in time for your needs, we say so straight away so you can make other arrangements.
The most common mistake we see is fixing the symptom on one laptop while the cause sits on the router, the mailbox or an expired licence. We check the shared pieces first.

sections.h2: The checks behind IT support
p: On IT support we work through four checks and write each one into the visit note: devices, users and accounts listed before work starts; fault reproduced and the cause written down; fix tested with the person who reported it; handover note of changes and remaining risks. If one of them shows a problem outside the urgent IT Support scope, it is reported and quoted separately rather than fixed without agreement.

sections.h2: Before you book urgent IT Support
p: Urgent requests are triaged by impact. A whole office unable to send email or reach the shared drive is handled differently from one slow laptop. Telling us how many people are affected helps us suggest the right first step.

While waiting, check the simple things we would ask about anyway: is the router showing its normal lights, has the broadband provider posted an outage, and does the fault affect wired and wireless devices or only one of them.

sections.h2: Who asks for IT support
p: Property businesses have a particular mix of kit: a handful of laptops, a shared printer, a router supplied by the broadband provider, a door-entry or CCTV recorder on the same network, and software for tenancies, rent and maintenance tickets. We look at that whole picture before changing anything, because a fix for one device can break another on a small network.

sections.h2: Urgent IT Support in different buildings
p: Landlords and HMO operators. Landlords often run a small business from home or a site office, with broadband in each property and a CCTV recorder or door-entry panel on the same router. IT support keeps the landlord's own systems apart from tenant broadband, so a tenant problem never becomes a business outage.

Offices and serviced suites. In a small office a single faulty laptop, printer or mailbox can stop a whole team. IT support looks at the shared pieces first: the router, the switch under the desk, the printer's address and the licences, because those are the parts that break several people's day at once.

Managed blocks and commercial buildings. Managing agents in blocks and mixed-use buildings deal with site offices, concierge desks and plant-room systems that need a working connection. IT support records who owns each device and contract so the managing agent, the freeholder and the tenants are not paying for the same thing twice.

sections.h2: Quotes, access and your data
p: Every IT job is price on application. We ask how many users and devices are involved, which systems the business relies on, whether there is an existing provider or contract, and what has already been tried. The written quote then says what is in scope, what is excluded and whether the work is onsite, remote or both.

What changes the price for IT support: the number of users and devices, whether the work can be done remotely, how many sites are involved, the state of existing documentation and passwords, any licences or hardware needed, and whether work has to happen outside normal office hours. All of these are listed on the quote, which is price on application.

On site we work around the people using the systems. Changes that will interrupt staff are agreed first, and anything that needs a restart is planned for a quiet moment. We do not install software or change settings beyond the agreed scope without asking.

CCTV recorders and door-entry panels exposed to the internet with default passwords are a frequent finding in managed buildings.

sections.h2: The checks behind network security
p: On network security we work through four checks and write each one into the visit note: external exposure reviewed; guest, staff and building systems separated; admin access secured; firmware and rules kept current. sections.h2: Who asks for network security
p: In managed buildings the network often carries more than computers. Door entry, CCTV recorders, access control panels, lift lines, alarm signalling and smart meters can all share switches and cabling. We map those before any change so that a firewall rule or a switch swap does not cut off a system someone depends on.

Blocks and managed buildings. Blocks carry building systems on the network: door entry, access control, CCTV and sometimes lift or alarm signalling. Network security maps those systems before any change and agrees with the managing agent which devices must never lose connection.

Shops, warehouses and yards. Card terminals, tills, stock scanners and yard cameras all need a connection that stays up. Network security in commercial premises plans for distance, dust and heat as well as the number of devices.

paragraphs: Network installation designs and fits the wired network for an office, block or HMO: router or firewall, switches, cabling, access points and the settings that tie them together.

On a network Installation job the order of work is: survey of rooms, users and devices; then equipment and cabling specified in writing; then network configured and tested; and finally handover of logins, layout and settings. Each step is written into the visit note so the client can see what was done and what is left.

Before the job we ask for photos of the comms cupboard and router, the broadband provider's details, a rough floor plan, and a list of other systems on the network such as CCTV recorders, door entry and card payment terminals.
Buying switches before planning the cabling and power often means a second visit. The survey avoids that.

Not included unless the quote says so: broadband or leased-line contracts, provider equipment, electrical supply work, builder's work in ceilings and walls, and fire-stopping where cables pass through compartment walls.

A network diagram, device list and admin credentials are handed to the client. After the job the client keeps the configuration backups, the diagram and the admin credentials. If another engineer takes over later, the record lets them start without guesswork.

Office tenants, building owners, managing agents and HMO landlords call us when the network is slow, keeps dropping, or has grown device by device until nobody knows what is plugged into what. New fit-outs and refurbishments also need a network designed before the ceilings close.

On site we agree a change window before touching live equipment, take configuration backups, and test business systems such as card terminals, door entry and CCTV before and after. Nothing is unplugged in a comms cupboard without labelling it first.

What changes the price for network installation: the number of devices and switch ports, whether new cabling is needed, the equipment brand, the number of networks to separate, how much documentation already exists, and any work that must be done outside trading hours. The quote is price on application and lists each item.
Offices. Office networks grow one switch at a time. For network installation we trace each cable, label each port and remove the loops and spare switches under desks that slow everyone down.

HMOs and shared houses. In HMOs the network has to serve several households fairly. Network installation separates tenant traffic from landlord devices and keeps the broadband router, any CCTV recorder and the door-entry panel on their own segments.

Blocks and managed buildings. Blocks carry building systems on the network: door entry, access control, CCTV and sometimes lift or alarm signalling. Network installation maps those systems before any change and agrees with the managing agent which devices must never lose connection.
